name: Greater Manchester
description: Greater Manchester is a metropolitan county in North West England centred on Manchester and surrounded by a dense network of towns and cities. It is one of Britain's major economic and cultural regions, with a strong industrial heritage and an increasingly diversified modern economy.

places.name: Oldham
places.description: A former cotton-spinning town in Greater Manchester that was once the most productive cotton-milling town in the world, its Victorian mill architecture still a defining feature.

places.name: Wigan
places.description: A former coal-mining town in Greater Manchester, its identity shaped by centuries of mining, textiles, and a resilient working-class culture.

places.name: Bolton
places.description: A former cotton-spinning town in Greater Manchester, home to Bolton Wanderers football club and Smithills Hall, one of the oldest manor houses in the North West.

places.name: Bury
places.description: A market town in Greater Manchester famous for its indoor market and black pudding, with a strong textile and papermaking industrial past.

places.name: Manchester
places.description: A major Northern English city that drove the Industrial Revolution as the world's first industrialised city, today known for its music scene, football rivalry, and vibrant Northern Quarter.

places.name: Rochdale
places.description: A former cotton-milling town in Greater Manchester, birthplace of the Co-operative Movement, founded here by the Rochdale Pioneers in 1844.

places.name: Salford
places.description: A city in Greater Manchester on the banks of the River Irwell, transformed from industrial docklands into MediaCityUK, now home to BBC and ITV studios at Salford Quays.

places.name: Stockport
places.description: A town in Greater Manchester famous for its Victorian railway viaduct, one of the largest brick structures in Europe, and its historic hatting industry.

places.name: Tameside
places.description: A district in Greater Manchester made up of former mill towns including Ashton-under-Lyne and Stalybridge, shaped by the cotton industry and the Pennine hills at its eastern edge.

places.name: Trafford
places.description: A district in Greater Manchester covering Old Trafford, home to Manchester United's stadium, and the Imperial War Museum North.
